newsitem.title: DENMARK: Sophus Berendsen seen sound, despite dip.
newsitem.headline: Sophus Berendsen seen sound, despite dip.

text.p: Danish holding company Sophus Berendsen is still sound and its share worth buying, despite setbacks due to losses in its Electronics and Data division, analysts said on Tuesday.
"I am completely sure that things will go much better," an analyst who asked not to be identified told Reuters.
Sophus dived seven percent on Monday after forecasting 1996 core profit down to 145 million crowns from 1995's 275 million.
But the forecast excluded earnings from associated companies such as Britain's Rentokil, which contributed 533 crowns to Sophus' overall first-half pre-tax profit of 640 million.

"(Electronics and Data) is only a small part of the company. The majority of its earnings still come from its stake in Rentokil," the analyst said, adding that he thought the share, sent down to 675 crowns on Monday, should be nearer 800.
It hit a year-high of 805 crowns in August.

An economist said that Sophus was far above its February low of 609 crowns and that other companies had rallied from worse positions, such as cleaner ISS which posted a two billion crown first-half loss due to false accounting in a U.S. unit.
"Look at ISS, it lost 50 times as much as Sophus in May and now its share is higher than it was before," he said.
As closing time approached on Tuesday Sophus had already recovered a good deal of Monday's losses, climbing 19 crowns to 694 crowns.
"It's a classic correction," a dealer said.
